title: Acts Chapter 22 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 22 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 22 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 22.

questions.question: In Acts 22, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: A great light shone from heaven
Paul identifies himself as a Jew
questions.explanation: Paul begins his defense by addressing the crowd in Acts 22:1.

questions.question: What language did Paul speak to the crowd in Acts 22?
questions.explanation: The crowd kept silence when they heard that Paul spoke in the Hebrew tongue, as stated in Acts 22:2.

questions.question: Where was Paul born?
questions.explanation: Paul identifies himself as a Jew born in Tarsus in Acts 22:3.

questions.question: Who taught Paul the perfect manner of the law?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions he was brought up at the feet of Gamaliel in Acts 22:3.

questions.question: What did Paul do to those who followed 'this way'?
questions.explanation: Paul states that he persecuted this way unto death in Acts 22:4.

questions.question: To whom did Paul receive letters to go to Damascus?
questions.explanation: Paul states that the high priest bears witness that he received letters from them in Acts 22:5.

questions.question: At what time did the great light shine around Paul?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions that the great light shone around him about noon in Acts 22:6.

questions.question: What did Paul hear while on the ground?
questions.explanation: Paul fell to the ground and heard a voice saying, 'Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?' in Acts 22:7.

questions.question: Who identified himself to Paul after he fell to the ground?
questions.explanation: The voice identified itself as Jesus of Nazareth in Acts 22:8.

questions.question: What did those who were with Paul see?
questions.explanation: Those with Paul saw indeed the light, but did not hear the voice in Acts 22:9.

questions.question: What did the Lord command Paul to do?
questions.explanation: The Lord commanded Paul to arise and go into Damascus in Acts 22:10.

questions.question: True or False: Paul was born in Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Acts 22:3 states that Paul was born in Tarsus, not Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: Paul was taught by Gamaliel.
questions.explanation: Acts 22:3 indicates that Paul was taught at the feet of Gamaliel.

questions.question: True or False: The high priest was not aware of Paul's actions.
questions.explanation: Acts 22:5 states that the high priest bears witness of Paul's actions.

questions.question: True or False: A great light shone around Paul while he was in Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Acts 22:6 states that the light shone around Paul as he approached Damascus, not while he was in Jerusalem.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 22 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 22 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Ananias say to Saul when he came to him?
questions.explanation: This is found in Acts 22:13, where Ananias came to Saul and addressed him directly, urging him to receive his sight.

questions.question: What does Acts 22:16 promise will happen if someone is baptized and calls on the name of the Lord?
options: Their sins will be washed away.
questions.correctAnswer: Their sins will be washed away.
questions.explanation: Acts 22:16 states that by being baptized and calling on the Lord's name, one's sins can be washed away, highlighting the importance of this act in the Christian faith.

questions.question: Who did the God of our fathers choose Saul to be?
questions.explanation: Acts 22:15 specifies that Saul was chosen to be a witness of what he had seen and heard, which is a central theme in his mission.

questions.question: What does Acts 22:17 indicate Saul was doing when he experienced a trance?
options: He was preaching in the streets.
He was praying in the temple.
questions.correctAnswer: He was praying in the temple.
questions.explanation: Acts 22:17 describes Saul as being in a trance while he prayed in the temple, which shows the importance of prayer in receiving divine guidance.

questions.question: What warning did Jesus give Saul in the trance?
questions.explanation: In Acts 22:18, Jesus tells Saul to make haste and get out of Jerusalem because the people would not accept his testimony, emphasizing the urgency of his mission.

questions.question: How did Saul respond when Jesus told him to arise and go into Damascus?
options: He was afraid and ran away.
questions.explanation: Acts 22:10 shows that Saul asked what he should do and was instructed to go into Damascus, showing his immediate obedience to the Lord's command.

questions.question: What did Saul say to the Lord about his past actions?
options: I was wrong to doubt you.
They know I imprisoned and beat believers.
questions.correctAnswer: They know I imprisoned and beat believers.
questions.explanation: In Acts 22:19, Saul acknowledges his past of persecuting Christians, which illustrates his understanding of the gravity of his former actions.

questions.question: What did Saul do after Ananias came to him?
options: He went to the temple to pray.
questions.explanation: Acts 22:13 explains that after Ananias spoke to Saul, he received his sight, marking a significant moment in Saul's conversion.

questions.question: What role did Stephen play in Saul's past according to Acts 22:20?
options: He was a mentor to Saul.
He was a martyr whose death Saul consented to.
questions.correctAnswer: He was a martyr whose death Saul consented to.
questions.explanation: Acts 22:20 states that Saul was present at the death of Stephen, indicating his prior involvement in the persecution of Christians.

questions.question: What does Acts 22:12 say about Ananias?
options: He was a devout man according to the law.
He was an enemy of Saul.
questions.correctAnswer: He was a devout man according to the law.
questions.explanation: Acts 22:12 describes Ananias as a devout man who had a good reputation among the Jews, highlighting his faithfulness and integrity.

questions.question: How did Saul feel about the actions he took against believers?
questions.explanation: Although not explicitly stated in this chapter, Saul's recognition of his past actions in Acts 22:19 and 20 implies a deep regret for his persecution of believers.

questions.question: What does true repentance involve according to the context of Acts 22?
questions.explanation: Acts 22:16 emphasizes that baptism and calling on the Lord's name are essential components of true repentance and faith.

questions.question: Is it true that Saul had a vision of Jesus before he received his sight?
questions.explanation: This is true as indicated in the narrative of Saul's conversion, where he encountered Jesus, which led to his blindness followed by healing.

questions.question: Is it true that Saul was happy about his previous actions against the Church?
questions.explanation: It is false; Saul expressed concern about his past actions, acknowledging the harm he caused to believers.

questions.question: Is it true that Ananias was known as a devout man among the Jews?
questions.explanation: This statement is false as Ananias is described in Acts 22:12 as a devout man with a good report among the Jews.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 22 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 22.

questions.question: What command did the Lord give Paul regarding the Gentiles?
options: Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles.
Stay: for I will send thee to the Jews.
Return: for I will send thee to Jerusalem.
Preach: for I will send thee to the synagogues.
questions.correctAnswer: Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles.
questions.explanation: This is the direct command from the Lord to Paul found in Acts 22:21, indicating the mission to the Gentiles.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the crowd when Paul mentioned sending the message to the Gentiles?
options: They were in shock and silence.
They lifted up their voices and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth.
questions.correctAnswer: They lifted up their voices and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth.
questions.explanation: The crowd's reaction is recorded in Acts 22:22, showing their vehement opposition to Paul’s message.

questions.question: What did the chief captain command regarding Paul after the crowd's uproar?
options: To be taken to the council.
questions.explanation: The chief captain's command is found in Acts 22:24 as he sought to understand the uproar against Paul.

questions.question: What question did Paul ask the centurion when he was about to be scourged?
options: Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?
Do you know who I am?
Are you afraid of the Jews?
Is this how you treat a prisoner?
questions.correctAnswer: Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?
questions.explanation: Paul's inquiry about his Roman citizenship is found in Acts 22:25, highlighting his legal rights.

questions.question: How did the centurion react to Paul's claim of Roman citizenship?
options: He went and told the chief captain.
questions.correctAnswer: He went and told the chief captain.
questions.explanation: The centurion's response is documented in Acts 22:26, indicating the seriousness of Paul's claim.

questions.question: What did Paul reveal about his Roman citizenship compared to the chief captain's?
options: I was granted it by the emperor.
questions.explanation: Paul's statement about his citizenship is in Acts 22:28, emphasizing his status as a free-born Roman citizen.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'ἀποστέλλω' (apostellō) in Acts 22:21 mean?
questions.explanation: 'ἀποστέλλω' means 'to send away,' which aligns with the command given to Paul to depart to the Gentiles.

questions.question: Which literary device is used when Paul recounts his conversion experience?
questions.explanation: The recounting of Paul's conversion includes a chiasm, emphasizing the pivotal moment of his transformation.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to Paul's mission to the Gentiles as mentioned in Acts 22:21?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:6 speaks of being a light to the nations, which parallels Paul's commission to bring the message to the Gentiles.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the theme of Paul being sent to the Gentiles as noted in Acts 22:21?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:16 articulates the Gospel being for the Jew first and also for the Gentile, reflecting Paul's mission.

questions.question: What precedes Paul's statement in Acts 22:21?
options: His vision on the road to Damascus.
The crowd's reaction to his speech.
His defense before the high priest.
questions.correctAnswer: The crowd's reaction to his speech.
questions.explanation: Acts 22:20 leads into the statement in verse 21, where Paul describes the command he received.

questions.question: What did Ananias say to Paul in Acts 22:13?
questions.explanation: In Acts 22:13, Ananias calls Paul 'Brother Saul' and commands him to receive his sight, marking a significant moment.

questions.question: In Acts 22, how does Paul's background as a Pharisee influence his defense?
options: It makes him more sympathetic to the crowd.
It allows him to speak Hebrew.
It gives him authority over the council.
It shows his education under Gamaliel.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows his education under Gamaliel.
questions.explanation: Paul's mention of being educated at the feet of Gamaliel in Acts 22:3 demonstrates his significant background.

questions.question: True or False: The chief captain was indifferent to Paul's Roman citizenship.
questions.explanation: The chief captain was afraid upon learning Paul was a Roman citizen, as noted in Acts 22:29.

questions.question: True or False: Paul was bound and uncondemned when he was about to be scourged.
questions.explanation: Acts 22:25 indicates that Paul was indeed bound and had not been condemned yet, raising the issue of legality regarding his scourging.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 22 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 22 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 22:16 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation involves baptism as a means to wash away sins
Salvation is achieved solely through works of the law
Salvation is predicated on ethnic heritage
Salvation is purely intellectual assent to doctrine
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation involves baptism as a means to wash away sins
questions.explanation: Acts 22:16 states, 'arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins,' indicating baptism’s role in the process of salvation as a means of cleansing from sin.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine election is taught in Acts 22:14?
options: God’s sovereign choice in revealing His will
Election is based on human merit
Election is contingent on ethnic lineage
Election excludes hearing the voice of God
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereign choice in revealing His will
questions.explanation: Acts 22:14 says, 'The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, that thou shouldest know his will,' emphasizing God’s sovereign election in revealing His redemptive plan.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of human sin is implied by Paul’s testimony in Acts 22:20?
options: Sin includes active participation and consent to persecution
Sin is limited to ignorance without moral culpability
Sin is only external and does not affect the heart
Sin can be justified by zeal for God
questions.correctAnswer: Sin includes active participation and consent to persecution
questions.explanation: Acts 22:20 highlights Paul’s consent to Stephen’s death, showing sin as active participation in wrongdoing, not merely passive ignorance.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 22:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: In Acts 22:7, God’s voice calls out to Paul about his persecution, showing God’s all-knowing awareness of human actions.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Acts 22:21 when God commissions Paul to the Gentiles?
questions.explanation: Acts 22:21 shows God directing Paul’s mission to the Gentiles, demonstrating divine sovereignty over salvation history.

questions.question: How does Acts 22:18 connect to the broader biblical theme of rejection of the Messiah by Israel?
options: It prepares for the Gentile mission due to Jewish rejection
It affirms universal acceptance of Jesus by Israel
It denies any opposition to the gospel
It emphasizes the permanent triumph of Jewish authorities
questions.correctAnswer: It prepares for the Gentile mission due to Jewish rejection
questions.explanation: Acts 22:18 records God instructing Paul to flee Jerusalem because his testimony will not be accepted, connecting to the theme of Jewish rejection and the gospel’s extension to Gentiles.

questions.question: How does Paul’s Roman citizenship in Acts 22:27–28 fulfill Old Testament promises about God’s providential care for His servants?
options: It shows God’s providential protection and advancement of His messengers
It indicates human political status as the basis for divine favor
It supports salvation by social privilege
It demonstrates God’s abandonment of Jewish believers
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God’s providential protection and advancement of His messengers
questions.explanation: Paul’s Roman citizenship, noted in Acts 22:27–28, exemplifies God’s providential arrangement to protect and empower His chosen servants in hostile contexts.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 22:4 and Acts 22:20 teach about human sin and repentance?
options: Human sin includes zealous persecution of the church, yet repentance leads to restoration
Sin is only external and cannot be forgiven
Repentance is unnecessary for those zealous for God
Sinful acts are always excused by religious zeal
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin includes zealous persecution of the church, yet repentance leads to restoration
questions.explanation: Acts 22:4 and 22:20 describe Paul’s previous persecution of Christians, showing sin’s severity; yet his testimony implies repentance and restoration in Christ.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 22:6 and Acts 22:9 teach about divine revelation and human perception?
options: Divine revelation can be perceived differently by individuals present
All observers receive identical supernatural knowledge
Divine revelation is always universally audible
Human perception is irrelevant to divine encounters
questions.correctAnswer: Divine revelation can be perceived differently by individuals present
questions.explanation: Acts 22:6–9 shows Paul sees and hears the voice of Jesus, but companions only see the light and do not hear the voice, highlighting subjective perception in revelation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 22:11 and Acts 22:13 teach about spiritual blindness and restoration through God’s appointed means?
options: Spiritual blindness is overcome by God’s appointed agent and means
Spiritual blindness is permanent and unchangeable
Restoration occurs only through human effort
Physical sight has no correlation to spiritual sight
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual blindness is overcome by God’s appointed agent and means
questions.explanation: Acts 22:11 and 22:13 recount Paul’s blindness after encountering divine glory and restoration through Ananias, God’s chosen instrument.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Paul fabricated his vision to justify his conversion. What does Acts 22:6–11 actually teach about the nature of this experience?
options: Paul’s vision was a literal, supernatural encounter with Jesus involving physical blindness
Paul’s vision was a purely psychological hallucination with no external effects
Paul’s vision was a metaphorical story invented to gain followers
Paul’s vision was a common mystical experience unrelated to Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: Paul’s vision was a literal, supernatural encounter with Jesus involving physical blindness
questions.explanation: Acts 22:6–11 describes a great light from heaven, a voice from Jesus, and Paul’s temporary blindness, indicating a real supernatural event.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine justice and human authority is taught in Acts 22:25–29?
options: Divine justice demands respect for human rights such as Roman citizenship
Human authorities have absolute power without restraint
Justice depends solely on mob opinion
Divine justice is irrelevant to earthly legal systems
questions.correctAnswer: Divine justice demands respect for human rights such as Roman citizenship
questions.explanation: Paul’s appeal to his Roman citizenship in Acts 22:25–29 protects him from unlawful scourging, showing divine justice operating through human legal rights.

questions.question: What doctrine about the role of prayer and divine revelation is taught in Acts 22:17?
options: Prayer can lead to divine revelation such as trances
Prayer is ineffective without loud public ceremony
Divine revelation is always verbal and audible
Prayer is irrelevant to receiving God’s guidance
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer can lead to divine revelation such as trances
questions.explanation: Acts 22:17 shows Paul praying in the temple and entering a trance, indicating prayer’s role in inviting divine revelation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 22:12 demonstrate in the character of Ananias?
questions.explanation: Ananias is described as 'a devout man according to the law, having a good report,' demonstrating God’s faithfulness in raising faithful servants.

questions.question: How does Acts 22:30 prepare for the coming trial and defense of Paul, connecting to the theme of gospel witness in hostile contexts?
options: It sets the stage for Paul’s public defense before Jewish authorities
It guarantees Paul’s immediate release without trial
It indicates the gospel will be universally accepted without opposition
It shows Paul abandoning his mission under pressure
questions.correctAnswer: It sets the stage for Paul’s public defense before Jewish authorities
questions.explanation: Acts 22:30 shows Paul being brought before the council, preparing for his defense and witness amid Jewish hostility, a key gospel theme.
